claims.text: A plasma-sprayed HEA coating induces selective surface enrichment of Cr and Nb on corrosion-sensitive steel.
The enriched Cr and Nb form a stable protective passivation layer.
The protective layer lowers steel corrosion rates under aggressive service conditions.
Equiatomic CrMoNbTiZr is an example of an HEA suitable for the proposed coating study.
(CoCrFeNi)95Nb5 can be deposited as a plasma-sprayed coating on a steel substrate.
A (CoCrFeNi)95Nb5 coating has high strength and corrosion resistance in its bulk state.
The proposed coating should be tested in NaCl-KCl-MgCl2 molten salts at 450–650 °C and in 3.5 wt.% NaCl solution.
These molten-salt and aqueous-chloride environments mimic chemical-processing and nuclear-power service conditions.
Plasma spraying produces rapid solidification and selective elemental segregation in the HEA coating.
Plasma spraying creates a duplex surface structure enriched in passivating elements and containing a coherent oxide-based barrier.
Rapid cooling and process-induced segregation drive Cr and Nb toward the coating surface.
Surface-enriched Cr and Nb oxidize to form stable, dense oxide layers.
The dense oxide layers impede corrosive attack by acting as protective passivation films.
HEA-coated steel will have a lower corrosion rate than uncoated steel under identical conditions.
HEA-coated steel will exhibit greater pitting resistance than uncoated steel.
HEA-coated steel will exhibit a more stable passivation film than uncoated steel.
The protective mechanism should remain effective for moderate exposure durations and typical chemical-processing or nuclear operating temperatures.
Very long exposures, irradiation, highly variable operation, or extreme conditions may degrade the coating or passivating layer.
XPS or EDS can test for surface enrichment, while polarization, cyclic polarization, and impedance measurements can compare corrosion behavior against an uncoated control.
The proposed falsification threshold is failure to obtain both measurable surface enrichment and at least a 20% statistically significant corrosion-rate improvement.
